# XY Forever serial protocol 1.31: transport, frames and constants

Part of the [XY Forever serial protocol 1.31](../PROTOCOL.md).

## Transport

How a tool reaches the protocol. `verified` is true for facts read from device sessions or the code, false for facts nobody has checked yet.

| Fact | Value | Verified | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| usb vendor id | `0x2367` | yes | teenage engineering: the stock serial identity (`scripts/usb_timeline.py`), used as fallback when a boot-time check fails |
| usb product id | `0x0021` | yes | the stock OS uses the same id with no serial interface (MTP, vendor class 0xFF; another mode is 0x8021, class 0x01), so a filter on both ids finds only XY Forever's service on the stock identity; a tool must accept this pair and `product_usb_ids` |
| product usb ids | `2367:0021` | yes | the composite (this CDC serial interface, MTP on interface 2) uses 2367:0021 (xyf_build.py MTP_USB_IDS); its device class 0xEF (IAD) distinguishes it from stock OS MTP and the stock serial fallback. XY Forever keeps this pair for good (#58) |
| usb product | `OP-XY (XY Forever)` | yes | the composite's product string (2026-11-23; macOS ioreg shows `OP_XY _XY Forever_`); the stock serial fallback and the stock recovery menu say `OP-XY Boot`; informational: filter on the ids |
| interface classes | `0x02, 0x0a` | yes | USB CDC: communications (0x02) and data (0x0A); on macOS the port is `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` |
| stream | `frames` | yes | the CDC data interface carries exactly the frame stream described here, in both directions, with no other framing; the simulator's TCP port carries the same bytes |
| line settings | `ignored` | yes | baud rate, parity, stop bits and flow control do not matter (an API that needs a baud rate may pass any); open the port raw (no echo, no line editing) |
| control lines | `unknown` | no | whether the device needs DTR or RTS set: `uv run xyf-host` leaves them as macOS sets them on open |
| usb serial number | `per unit` | yes | the OP-XY's own serial (the stock metadata's `serial`, 8 characters), which the stock USB stack sends in every mode, XY Forever's included (2026-11-23), and MTP's DeviceInfo repeats; never assume a value. Vendor id, product id and serial match in every mode, the product strings do not. Chrome keeps a Web Serial or WebUSB permission only for a device with a serial; on macOS (2026-11-23) one grant per API covers the OP-XY in every mode and across power cycles: Web Serial's one remembered port is also the stock recovery menu's `OP-XY Boot` port, which does not speak this protocol; Windows is untested ([USB identity](../hardware/usb-identity.md)) |
| simulator port | `7341` | yes | default TCP port of the device simulator (`uv run -m xy_forever.sim`, 127.0.0.1 only; its control port is a separate setting, 7342 by default), one client at a time |

## Frames

Every message, in both directions, is one frame:

| Offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `magic` | bytes[2] | ASCII `XF` (0x58 0x46) |
| 2 | `type` | u8 | message type: a request (< 0x80), its reply (request type + 0x80) or an event |
| 3 | `seq` | u8 | chosen by the tool for each request; the reply carries the same value; events use 0 |
| 4 | `length` | u32 | payload bytes, at most `max_payload` |
| 8 | `payload` | rest | `length` bytes |
| 8 + length | `crc` | u32 | CRC-32 of magic, type, seq, length and payload |

The CRC is the zlib CRC-32 (polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial value and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, as Python's zlib.crc32) over every byte before it.
Example, `hello` with seq 1: `58 46 01 01 00 00 00 00 4c 8d 06 32`.

Payload fields are packed without gaps. Types: `u8`, `u16`, `u32` unsigned little-endian; `bytes[N]` exactly N bytes; `cstr` text ending in one NUL; `text` text
to the end of the payload, no NUL; `rest` raw bytes to the end of the payload. Each text field names its encoding (ASCII or UTF-8; see the [rules](rules.md)).
Optional fields come last and are all present or all absent. A reply payload is a `u32` status followed by the fields listed for it.

## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `header_bytes` | 8 | magic, type, seq and length |
| `trailer_bytes` | 4 | the CRC-32 |
| `max_payload` | 4160 | largest payload in either direction; a frame announcing more is treated as noise |
| `max_data` | 4096 | largest file or image data in one reply |
| `max_read` | 1024 | largest `length` of a ranged `file.read`, and the most data `screen.read` returns per reply |
| `put_chunk` | 1024 | data bytes per `stage.data` request that tools should send: the device's USB receive buffer holds 2048 bytes, and a 4 KiB frame overflowed it (no reply) |
| `max_path` | 240 | largest device path, including its NUL |
| `max_stage` | 7340032 | largest staged image (7 MiB) |
| `max_log_text` | 200 | largest text of a `log` event |
| `idle_reset_ms` | 250 | the device drops a partial frame once its receive buffer has been empty for this long |
| `max_hello` | 256 | largest `hello` text (240 before 1.25, 224 before 1.23, 200 before 1.15); a build's text is fixed but for its run-time parts (221 bytes in the product build without stage 2, nothing asked, serial on), checked when it is compiled |
